contentHtml:
Bhopal: The Madhya Pradesh Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a public health warning against two Pakistan-manufactured skin-lightening creams, Gori Beauty Cream and Chandni Whitening Cream, following concerns over excessive levels of mercury and other heavy metals. The department has advised consumers across the state to immediately discontinue the use and purchase of these products due to potential health risks.

According to the health advisory issued by the office of the Controller, Food and Drug Administration, Madhya Pradesh, the two cosmetic products contain heavy metals, particularly mercury, in concentrations exceeding the permissible limits. The department also clarified that neither product has obtained the mandatory import registration or licence from the competent regulatory authority, making their sale in India unauthorised.

The public notice, dated November 14, stated that the matter was brought to the attention of the state authorities by the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) and the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO). The central regulatory authorities had initially flagged the products on September 8, highlighting concerns regarding their composition and safety.

The FDA has cautioned that prolonged exposure to mercury through skin-lightening preparations can lead to serious health complications. Continuous application of such products may adversely affect kidney function and the nervous system, apart from causing skin-related problems. Consumers who have already purchased Gori Beauty Cream, Chandni Whitening Cream or products marketed under similar names have been instructed to stop using them immediately.

Mercury-containing skin-whitening cosmetics have previously attracted regulatory attention in several countries. Mercury is sometimes used in skin-lightening preparations because of its ability to interfere with melanin production. However, repeated exposure can result in the accumulation of the toxic metal in the human body, increasing the risk of adverse health effects.

Meanwhile, enforcement action was initiated in Indore ahead of the public advisory. On Friday, drug department officials conducted searches at two premises suspected of selling the unauthorised cosmetic products. During the inspection at The Beauty Bar in Ranipura, officials seized a few packets of the cream. A separate search at Padmashree Agency in Chhawani resulted in the recovery of approximately 300 packets of Gori Beauty Cream, with an estimated market value of around Rs 1.5 lakh. The seized packages reportedly carried labels indicating that they were manufactured in Pakistan.

The Madhya Pradesh FDA has declared the sale of both products unauthorised within the state. However, the department has not disclosed whether criminal proceedings have been initiated against the concerned sellers or provided details regarding the supply chain through which the products entered the Indore market.

To strengthen enforcement and prevent further circulation, the department has urged residents to report any instances of the sale or distribution of these creams. Complaints can be submitted through the dedicated email address, cfdamp@rediffmail.com, or directly to the drug inspector concerned in the respective district. The New Indian Express reports that the department has also emphasised the importance of checking cosmetic product labels before purchase.

The FDA has advised consumers to exercise caution while purchasing cosmetic products. Buyers should verify essential label information, including the manufacturing licence number, manufacturer’s name and complete address, batch number, manufacturing date and expiry date. In the case of imported cosmetics, consumers should additionally check for a valid import registration or licence number and details of the foreign manufacturer, including its name and address.
